text:
samir: Heads-up — Support got a high-priority from Acme (SUP-4512). p95 on /v1/generate jumped from ~450ms to ~1.2s for them starting ~02:15 UTC last night. eu-west-1, redwood-13b-quant.

jessica-support: Customer says this regressed after the 2026-03-02 model routing change. They attached traces and a short repro payload. Customer impact: their real-time chat sees slow UX and some timeouts.

kevin-eng: Thanks. Can you paste the trace links and the exact request rates they were sending? Need concurrency and batch sizes.

jessica-support: Trace link: https://tracing.internal/acme/SUP-4512. They report sustained 120 RPS with bursts to 300 RPS and avg request length ~400 tokens.

tracing-bot: New trace uploaded: trace_id=acme-20260302-17, spans=820, top-latency-span=kv-cache-miss (450ms).

kevin-eng: kv-cache-miss is notable. 13B quant should benefit from KV cache. If cache miss rate jumped that explains p95. Any recent infra/deploys around 02:00 UTC?

opsbot: deploy-bot: Routing change rollout `route-policy/2026-03-02-model-weight-adjust` completed at 01:58 UTC (all regions).

samir: That rollout adjusted traffic weights to prefer redwood-13b-quant over 7b for high-quality tier. Might have increased cold KVs.

elaine-product: From product side: Acme is on enterprise plan, agreed SLOs. This is a priority customer ask — we need mitigation + RCA and then decide backlog priority for a longer fix.

kevin-eng: Initial triage: 1) Verify cache warmup behavior after routing change. 2) Check model shard sizing and if dedicated pools were underprovisioned. 3) Run repro at same RPS in staging with same routing policy.

maria-sales: FYI Acme is threatening to pause their rollout if latency not fixed in 48h. Sales needs a short mitigation path to tell customer.

kevin-eng: Short mitigation we can do ASAP: rollback routing weights to previous percentages (route back some traffic to 7b) or enable cached prefixes/pinned KV for their tenant on Dedicated (if on Dedicated). Which one is faster?

samir: They are on Hosted API (multi-tenant). Rollback is fastest and lowest-risk. Ops — can you rollback routing policy for eu-west-1?

opsbot: ops-request: rollback scheduled. Who approves?

elaine-product: I approve rollback for eu-west-1 for 2 hours while we validate. Make it a staged rollback with metrics monitor.

opsbot: rollback-job created: rollback-id rb-179450-1. ETA 8 minutes.

tracing-bot: Alert configured: p95(/v1/generate, customer=Acme) > 900ms for 5m.

kevin-eng: I'll repro load against staging with the same quantized model and routing weights. Putting together a small script. Attaching quick repro command:

kevin-eng: ```bash
wrk -t16 -c300 -d5m --latency https://staging-redwood/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' -s scripts/acme_workload.lua
```

jessica-support: I've told the customer we'll put a short mitigation in place and follow up within 2 hours with a plan.

samir: Post-rollback — we need an RCA ticket with scope: why cache miss rate increased (routing + shard warming), whether kernel selection or quantization changed performance, and backlog item to add tenant-aware pre-warming for high-RPS customers.

elaine-product: Acceptance criteria for backlog item: (a) reproducible test that shows <200ms added p95 for warm cache, (b) automated pre-warm on route changes, (c) docs & runbook. Priority: P0 for the next sprint if RCA confirms routing-induced misses.

kevin-eng: Assigning owner: INF-789 (created). Owner: kevin-eng. I'll update with repro results and perf graphs.

maria-sales: Thanks — I'll notifiy Acme contact that mitigation is rolling and we'll follow up with timeline.

opsbot: rollback complete at 1794509440. Metrics monitor: p95 dropped from 1.18s -> 520ms within 10 minutes.

tracing-bot: New trace captured post-rollback: kv-cache-miss rate down 78%.

kevin-eng: Good signal. Will still run staged experiments to verify warmup windows. If safe, we'll add a quick guard in routing to avoid rapid weight shifts for high-RPS tenants.

elaine-product: Next steps: 1) kevin-eng completes RCA ticket INF-789 with root cause and short/medium-term fixes. 2) Product scope decision meeting EOD to decide if fix goes into next sprint or needs hotfix. 3) Sales to keep Acme updated.

samir: Thanks everyone. If anything changes or we see re-regression, ping @kevin-eng and ops on-call. :thumbsup:
